result.title: SceneBound: How Much Should a Streaming 3D Reconstruction Model Remember?
result.summary: Streaming 3D reconstruction models keep past video frames in a recurrent state, fast weights from test-time training, or a key-value (KV) cache. Each written frame shifts the coordinate frame of later cameras or occupies GPU memory. Training-free rules decide what to write from a signal of the current frame. How much they write accounts for their mean accuracy: spending the update budget of a gate at uniformly spaced frames, with no signal, matches nine published gates, and the budget bounds the drift of the state wherever the writes fall. We propose SceneBound, a training-free rule that writes a frame only when its predicted camera pose lies at least a fixed radius from every stored keyframe. Its keyframe count stays within a constant factor of the covering number of the visited poses, the fewest views that keep a keyframe near every camera, so the count grows with the places visited and stays flat when the camera returns. In large scenes, SceneBound closes a submap once decoding its first frame again reveals drift. SceneBound uses one radius across four released models and three memory types. In the recurrent state of CUT3R and the KV cache of StreamVGGT, it achieves the lowest mean trajectory error among the published training-free rules we evaluate, in one pass and over nine passes of a scene, where its keyframes grow by 3% to 6%.

AI.brief_summary: 研究流式 3D 重建中循环状态、fast weights 或 KV cache 应写入多少历史帧，提出无需训练的 SceneBound：仅当预测相机位姿与已存关键帧距离超过固定半径时才写入，并在大场景中依据漂移关闭子图；在四个模型、三种记忆类型上以单遍处理取得最低平均轨迹误差。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「写入预算—状态漂移界」与基于覆盖数的稀疏写入规则，可能为 LVR 中 latent 记忆何时更新、如何控制状态陈旧与计算成本提供可核查的类比线索，但该文本身不涉及多模态推理。
